Using AI to grade or give feedback to written responses is a very bad idea in my opinion. The only reason you would consider it is because you do not have enough TAs/time to grade written responses manually, but this argument falls for the fallacy that giving students more work is necessarily better for us or our learning. Output/quantity should not be taken as an indicator of quality. Completing a higher workload is no proof of understanding the material. Give us more conceptual questions and essay style questions but then reduce other busy work and reassign TA hours so that these conceptual questions can be properly graded with good feedback. By adding more work and using AI to grade it, all you are doing is leading us to a world where students will AI generate the entirety of their work and all that AI generated work will be graded by AI. This helps no one.

The way you would solve for the work of the air resistance in this case is by first ignoring it and converting all of the kinetic energy to get the theoretical gravitational potential energy if no air resistance was present. You would then compute the actual gravitation potential energy at the maximum height the ball achieves. You could then find the work done by air resistance by subtracting the actual gravitational potential energy from the theoretical gravitational potential energy. (W_surr = U_theoretical-U_actual). We are to assume the work done by air resistance is the same coming down, which means we can now convert the actual gravitational potential energy into kinetic energy and then subtract the value we got for W_surr from the kinetic energy to get the actual kinetic energy on the way down. We then simply plug in v = \sqrt(2KE/m)
